newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - May 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Frank Dobson, the new Health Secretary, told the annual conference of the Royal College of Nursing in Harrogate that Labour would be sticking to its election commitment that there would be no big pay rises for public sector workers.
US FIRMS PLAN BIG BOOST FOR CITY JOBS

Major American finance houses, including Goldman Sachs and Merrill Lynch, are looking to acquire a further 1.4 million square feet of office space in the City and in Central London, according to a survey by the chartered surveyors Chesterton. This level of increase means the firms will be looking to recruit 9400 extra staff.
DOLLAR PERKS UP AHEAD OF FED RATES SUMMIT
An initial decline in the dollar was brought to a halt today as traders' attention was caught by a possible increase in interest rates by the Federal Reserve.
Christopher Sharples, who founded Intercom Data Systems with 15,000 stg in 1982, is set to make a profit of up to 8 million stg when the software company floats on the Stock Exchange in June.
HOW KIWIS BEAT US ON ROAD TO REFORM

Far from being Britain's backward little sister, New Zealand has been way ahead of Britain in reform. While in Britain Gordon Brown has only just given the Bank of England the power to set interest rates, in New Zealand the central bank's governor has to report six-monthly and can be sacked for failing to meet inflation targets set in 1989 at between 0 percent and 2 percent annually.
